notes: §1985:XIII.3.11.2 prints the clause as 'COLUMN NUMBER IS integer-1' (NUMBER and IS optional), integer-1 giving the leftmost column (§1985:XIII.3.11.4 GR2). The superset rule reportColumnClause/reportColumnOperand parses it and VersionConformancePass.VisitReportColumnClause refuses at 85 (COBOL0900, ReportMultiColumn2002) every 2002 form: COL/COLS/COLUMNS/NUMBERS spellings, LEFT/CENTER/RIGHT, PLUS or '+' operand, more than one operand; ConstantIntegerText refuses an identifier operand (COBOL1547, the witness). Probes at 85: COLUMN NUMBER IS 3, COLUMN 3, COLUMN IS 3, COLUMN NUMBER 3 each print HELLO at column 3; COL/COLS/COLUMNS/NUMBERS/LEFT/CENTER/RIGHT/PLUS 2/+ 2/+3/'1 9' all COBOL0900 (accepted at 2023); COLUMN 0 COBOL2386, -1 and ARE and 1.5 parse errors, COLUMN written twice COBOL2423, group entry COBOL2247; OCCURS in a report entry COBOL0900; signed/edited/ALL/SPACES and ref-modified SOURCE items print at their columns (-ZZ9 of -12 '- 12', S99V9 TRAILING SEPARATE '120-').

next.reason: 1985: 'COLUMN NUMBER IS integer-1'. §2023:13.18.14.2 Format 1 (report-writer) accepts it with the same meaning (absolute column, LEFT assumed: §2023:13.18.14.3 SR9 'If any of the operands is absolute and neither LEFT, CENTER, nor RIGHT is specified, LEFT is assumed') and adds the COL/COLUMNS/COLS synonyms (§2023:13.18.14.3 SR1), LEFT/CENTER/RIGHT, relative 'PLUS integer-2' and a multiple COLUMN clause (§2023:13.18.14.3 SR10). No 1985 rule allows those forms. CHANGED (looser).
